data.cultural_impact: The name Rauhah reflects a value and characteristic deeply embedded within the Islamic faith and culture. Calmness and peace are considered virtues that should be pursued in both daily life and worship. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Allah's Messenger (pbuh) said, 'The strong believer is better and dearer to Allah than the weak believer, and both are in paradise. Explanation of Sahih Bukhari by Dr. Muhammad Muhsin Khan, Vol. 7, Book 62, Number 45." By giving their child the name Rauhah, parents are imbuing them with the desire and aspiration to embody the trait of peace and tranquility.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, peace and tranquility are not only external traits but also internal ones. A soul at peace corresponds to a heart filled with the love and fear of Allah. The Caliph Umar Bin Al-Khattab once stood weeping, and when asked the reason for his tears he replied, "My sins are weighing heavy upon me, and I am afraid that Allah will expose me in this Assembly [heaven]." (Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah). The name Rauhah therefore signifies a spiritual journey towards a calm and peaceful existence in both this life and the hereafter.
